In 1990, the most famous tower in Italy was closed, because it was falling over.
The Leaning Tower of Pisa had been tilting since the 1170s, when it began to sink into the soft ground under it.
By 1990 it leaned further than ever, so the engineers had to act.
First, cables were tied around the tower, and anchored far across the square.
Then they stacked 870 tonnes of lead weights on its high side, to pull it back.
But the real trick was underground.
They drilled beneath the high side, and drew the soil out, a little at a time.
With the ground gone, the high side slowly settled, and the whole tower leaned back.
About 45 centimetres, back to where it stood in 1838.
In 2001, the tower opened again, still leaning, on purpose.
